A more detailed and updated version:

"""
1. **DepthCameraSensor** and **RgbdCameraSensor**: `<camera><clip><near>` is
   now only the near clip plane of the rendering frustum. Geometry closer
   than it is not rendered and does not occlude, so a sensor can see through
   its own housing: the depth image and point cloud report the surface
   behind it, or `+inf` if there is none. In 10.X that geometry was reported
   as `-inf`. This applies to every depth and RGBD camera, including those
   without a `<depth_camera>` element, and a camera without
   `<depth_camera><clip><near>` never reports `-inf`. To keep reporting
   obstacles closer than a minimum range as `-inf`, set
   `<camera><depth_camera><clip><near>` to that range and set
   `<camera><clip><near>` to a smaller value, e.g. the size of the sensor
   housing.
1. **DepthCameraSensor** and **RgbdCameraSensor** forward
   `<camera><depth_camera><clip><near>` and `<far>` to
   `gz::rendering::DepthCamera::SetDepthNearClipPlane` and
   `SetDepthFarClipPlane`. Geometry between `<camera><clip><near>` and
   `<depth_camera><clip><near>` is reported as `-inf`, and geometry beyond
   `<depth_camera><clip><far>` as `+inf`; `<depth_camera><clip><far>` may be
   larger than `<camera><clip><far>`. In 10.X, **DepthCameraSensor** ignored
   `<depth_camera><clip>`, and **RgbdCameraSensor** applied it only inside
   the `<camera><clip>` range. A `<depth_camera><clip><near>` smaller than
   `<camera><clip><near>` is ignored with a warning; lower
   `<camera><clip><near>` instead.
1. `DepthCameraSensor::NearClip()` and `DepthCameraSensor::FarClip()` return
   the `<depth_camera><clip>` distances, or the `<camera><clip>` distances
   when those are not set. In 10.X they returned the `<camera><clip>`
   distances. Use `DepthCamera()->NearClipPlane()` and `FarClipPlane()` to
   get the frustum clip planes.
"""
